trust_decision.summary: lilxml decides how much of an untrusted, unbounded XML token (tag, end tag, attribute name) is copied into the caller-supplied error buffer ynot[]. At the pinned commit it uses unbounded sprintf, and callers pass buffers as small as 512 bytes.

landing_point.why: The summary names indiserver and XML tag parsing. MsgQueue::readFromFd passes the socket chunk to parseXMLChunk with a stack err[1024], so an engineer goes from there to the sprintf calls in lilxml.cpp oneXMLchar.

same parser; other oneXMLchar error formats (1115, 1130, 1142, 1155, 1269, 1294) and early-EOF messages (302, 396)
new XML_ERROR_SIZE public constant for every caller of the lilxml public API

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: libs/indibase/inditelescope.cpp:2070, libs/indibase/indidome.cpp:1804, libs/indibase/defaultdevice.cpp:259, drivers/auxiliary/joystick.cpp:729 (park, nickname and calibration file reloads with 512-byte static errmsg buffers; obsolete/skywatcherAltAzSimple.cpp:533 is a legacy_path variant)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names indiserver network parsing, so the local park, nickname and calibration files a driver writes and rereads look like trusted local state and outside the network attack surface. Likewise the crackDN/dispatch messages are 'not lilxml', and their buffers are 1024-2048 bytes, which looks big enough.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: lilxml must keep accepting arbitrarily long tag names, attribute values and pcdata (growString grows without limit; BLOB base64 payloads are large), and an empty ynot[] must keep meaning 'need more input' for chunked parsing. A fix that rejects long tokens or puts a placeholder error into ynot on partial input breaks BLOB transfer and incremental parsing.

O6_input_shapes: closing tag that does not match the opening tag (both names long)
attribute with no value (long attribute name)
single bogus character errors in tag, attribute and end-tag states
caller buffer of 512 bytes (static) versus 1024 bytes (stack)
